text:
jordan: Heads up: tenant-42 private VPC saw a sustained 4x P95 spike around 14:05 UTC. Looks like an egress/SNAT issue compounded by the kernel selector falling back — pasting quick notes and logs below.

infra-bot: Alert: high latency detected for tenant-42 (p95 > 3s). Auto-remediate policies did not fire because dedicated capacity threshold not reached.

anya: Any quick repro or timeline?

jordan: Timeline: 14:00 normal, 14:02 large embedding ingestion from job-embed-9 (many long-lived streaming client -> backend calls), 14:03 conntrack entries climbing, 14:04 ephemeral ports exhausted -> many flows NATted to same port, 14:04:30 kernel selector started logging fallback to generic kernel path (increased per-token latency), 14:05 P95 spikes.

jordan: Logs snippet:```
[2026-03-18T14:04:29Z] kv_kernel_select(): model=redwood-7b, preferred=kv_optimized_kernel, result=fallback_kernel, reason=conntrack_pressure
[2026-03-18T14:04:29Z] netfilter: conntrack_count=262140 (max=262144)
[2026-03-18T14:04:30Z] snat: ephemeral_ports_exhausted tenant=tenant-42
[2026-03-18T14:04:31Z] batching: reduced batch_size from 32 -> 12 due to latency_guard
```

liam: Checked node metrics: conntrack table at 100%, /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max=262144, ss -s shows many TIME_WAIT/ESTAB entries pinned to a handful of SNAT ports. SNAT port range is default 32768-60999 — not enough given long-lived streams and high fanout.

jordan: Also saw a KV cache hit-rate collapse during window: profiling output:```
kv_cache: pre-spike hit_rate=0.92
kv_cache: during-spike hit_rate=0.27
kernel-profiling: kv_kernel_select latency p95 increased 8x -> ~420ms
```

ryan: That explains throughput drop: more requests hit fallback kernel (slower path) and batches shrank unpredictably, so tokens/sec dropped. Any quick mitigations we can roll?

anya: Mitigations I want to try now (canary):
- expand SNAT port range on affected nodes to 10240-65535
- temporarily bump nf_conntrack_max to 524288
- force kernel_selection.flag=prefer_optimized for tenant-42 (runtime override) to pin to optimized path while we clear conntrack
- reduce max_batch_size to 8 for embedding-heavy flows to avoid large prefix pressure

liam: I'll apply SNAT range + conntrack bump to two canary nodes and patch runtime flag for tenant-42. Doing that now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: canary/egress-snat-adjust -> nodes node-104,node-107

deploy-bot: Deploy success: canary/egress-snat-adjust -> nodes node-104,node-107

jordan: Canary telemetry: p95 back to normal on canary nodes within ~45s of change. KV cache hit-rate recovered to ~88% and kernel selector chose optimized path again. Rolling to rest of cluster in 5m.

ryan: Follow-ups for postmortem:
- add heuristics in kernel selector to avoid fallback during transient conntrack_pressure (short window hysteresis)
- add metric alert on SNAT port exhaustion and conntrack utilization per-tenant
- implement eviction policy for long-lived non-kv traffic (idle-ttl < 40s) or refresh clients to avoid port pinning
- document runbook steps (SNAT range, conntrack bump, runtime pinning)

anya: I'll open the PR for runtime flag + runbook and schedule postmortem. Also suggests evaluating BPF-based NAT to reduce conntrack pressure.

liam: Notes: we should also consider increasing our default ephemeral port range and revisiting streaming client behavior (keepalives).

infra-bot: Monitoring: all canaries nominal, rolling to remaining nodes now.

jordan: Thanks team. I'll capture this in the incident doc and include the kernel selection profiling details.

anya: :thumbsup: will own follow-ups (PR + PM sync).
